q: 1. The flow is called rotational if its velocity normal to the plane of area is equal to ...............
explain: Vorticity is defined as the curl of the velocity vector, which is equal to twice the angular velocity (ω).

q: 2. For an irrotational flow, the equation (δ²φ/δx²) + (δ²φ/δy²) = 0 given by ...............
explain: This is the Laplace equation. If a velocity potential (φ) satisfies this equation, the flow is irrotational and incompressible.

q: 3. 'Flow net' can be drawn only if the flow is ...............
explain: A flow net is applicable only for irrotational (potential) flow where both stream functions and velocity potentials exist.

q: 4. If u, v, w are the components of the velocity v of moving particle, the equation u/dx = v/dy = w/dz represents ...............
explain: This is the general differential form for the path of a particle in three-dimensional space.

q: 5. In two dimensional flow the components of velocity are given by u = ax, v = by. The stream lines will be ...............
explain: By integrating dy/dx = v/u = (by)/(ax), we get a power relationship that represents a hyperbolic shape for the streamlines.

q: 6. In a two dimensional flow if the components of the velocity are u = ax, v = by, the point where no motion occurs, is known as ...............
explain: A stagnation point is defined as a point in the flow field where all velocity components (u, v, w) are zero.

q: 7. Energy equation is usually applicable to ...............
explain: Bernoulli's energy equation is derived assuming steady flow, meaning conditions at a point do not change with time.

q: 8. Bernoulli's equation assumes that ...............
explain: Bernoulli's principle relies on the assumptions of steady, irrotational, incompressible, and non-viscous (frictionless) flow.

q: 9. In a centriyugal pump casing, the flow of water leaving the impeller, is ...............
explain: Once the water leaves the impeller and enters the volute casing, it follows a free vortex path to convert kinetic energy into pressure energy.

q: 10. A pitot tube is used to measure ...............
explain: A pitot tube converts kinetic energy into potential energy at the stagnation point to determine the local velocity of the fluid.

q: 11. If the forces are due to inertia and gravity, and frictional resistance plays only a minor role, the design of the channels is made by comparing ...............
explain: Froude number is used for open channel designs where gravity is the primary driving force (e.g., spillways, canals).

q: 12. The following is not a laminar flow ...............
options: flow in beds in ground water
rise of water in plants through roots
flow of blood in the arteries of human body
explain: Flow in typical water supply pipe lines is usually turbulent due to high velocities and large diameters.

q: 13. The value of kinetic energy correction factor (α) for a laminar flow through a circular pipe, is ...............
explain: For laminar flow in a pipe, the velocity distribution is parabolic, leading to a kinetic energy correction factor (α) of exactly 2.0.

q: 14. The value of momentum correction factor (β) for a laminar flow through a circular pipe, is ...............
explain: The momentum correction factor (β) for laminar flow in a pipe is calculated as 4/3 (~1.33).

q: 15. To avoid vapourisation, pipe lines are laid over the ridge so that these are above the hydraulic gradient line not more than ...............
explain: To prevent cavitation and the release of dissolved air (which causes air locks), the summit of a pipeline (siphon) should not be more than 6.4 meters above the hydraulic gradient line.

q: 16. The phenomenon occurring in an open channel when a rapidly flowing stream abruptly changes to slowly flowing stream causing rise in water surface ...............
explain: A hydraulic jump occurs when supercritical flow (high velocity) transitions to subcritical flow (low velocity), resulting in significant energy dissipation and a rise in water level.

q: 17. The gases are considered incompressible when mach number ...............
explain: Gas flow is generally treated as incompressible if the Mach number is less than about 0.3, as density variations are negligible below this speed.

q: 18. The necessary condition for the flow to be steady is that
options: the velocity does not change from place to place
the velocity is constant at a point with respect to time
the velocity changes at a point with respect to time
explain: Steady flow is defined as the type of flow in which fluid characteristics like velocity, pressure, and density at a point do not change with time (dv/dt = 0).

q: 19. The necessary condition for the flow to be uniform is that
options: the velocity is constant at a point with respect to time
the velocity is constant in the flow field with respect to space
the velocity changes at a point with respect to time
explain: Uniform flow occurs when the velocity of flow does not change with respect to space (distance) at any given time (dv/ds = 0).

q: 20. A stream line is a line
options: which is along the path of a particle
which is always parallel to the main direction of flow
across which there is no flow
explain: By definition, the velocity vector is tangent to the streamline at every point; therefore, there is no component of velocity perpendicular to the streamline, meaning no flow crosses it.

q: 21. Bernoulli's theorem deals with the law of conservation of
explain: Bernoulli's theorem states that for an incompressible, non-viscous fluid in steady flow, the sum of pressure energy, kinetic energy, and potential energy per unit mass remains constant, following the law of conservation of energy.

q: 22. Continuity equation deals with the law of conservation of
explain: The continuity equation (A1V1 = A2V2) is based on the principle that mass can neither be created nor destroyed in a flow system, representing the conservation of mass.

q: 23. Irrotational flow means
options: the fluid does not rotate while moving
the fluid moves in straight lines
the net rotation of fluid-particles about their mass centres is zero
explain: Irrotational flow is a flow in which the fluid particles do not rotate about their own axes, meaning the curl of the velocity vector is zero.

q: 24. Bernoulli's equation is derived making assumptions that
options: the flow is uniform, steady and incompressible
the flow is non-viscous, uniform and steady
the flow is steady, non-viscous, incompressible and irrotational
explain: The standard derivation of Bernoulli's equation assumes the fluid is ideal (non-viscous), the flow is steady, incompressible, and occurs along a streamline (irrotational).

q: 25. If the velocity, pressure, density etc, do not change at a point with respect to time, the flow is called
explain: When fluid properties at a specific point remain constant regardless of time, the flow is categorized as steady flow.

q: 26. If the velocity, pressure, density etc., change at a point with respect to time, the flow is called
explain: If fluid parameters at any point vary as time progresses, the flow is known as unsteady flow.

q: 27. Vorticity is given by
explain: Vorticity is defined mathematically as the curl of the velocity vector, which is exactly equal to twice the angular velocity (rotation).

q: 28. The term V²/2g is known as
explain: In the Bernoulli equation, the term V²/2g represents the Kinetic Head, which is the kinetic energy of the fluid per unit weight.

q: 29. The term p/ρg is known as
explain: The term p/ρg represents the 'Pressure Head', which is the pressure energy of the fluid per unit weight of the fluid.

q: 30. The term Z is known as
explain: In Bernoulli's equation, Z represents the 'Datum Head' or 'Elevation Head', which is the potential energy per unit weight of the fluid.

q: 31. A flow is said to be laminar when
options: the fluid particles move in a zig-zag way
the fluid particles move in layers parallel to the boundary
explain: Laminar flow occurs when fluid particles move in smooth, well-defined paths or layers that do not cross each other.

q: 32. For the laminar flow through a circular pipe
options: the max velocity = 1.5 times the average velocity
the max velocity = 2.0 times the average velocity
the max velocity = 2.5 times the average velocity
explain: In fully developed laminar pipe flow (Hagen-Poiseuille flow), the maximum velocity at the center is exactly twice the average velocity across the section.

q: 33. The loss of pressure head for the laminar flow through pipes varies
options: as the inverse of the velocity
explain: According to the Hagen-Poiseuille equation for laminar flow, the head loss (hf) is given by (32μVL)/(ρgD²). This shows that head loss is directly proportional to the first power of the velocity (V).

q: 34. For the laminar flow through a pipe, the shear stress over the cross-section
options: varies inversely as the distance from the centre
varies directly as the distance from the surface
varies directly as the distance from the centre
explain: In a circular pipe, the shear stress distribution is linear, starting from zero at the center and reaching a maximum at the pipe wall. It is directly proportional to the radial distance (r) from the center.

q: 35. For the laminar flow between two parallel plate
explain: For laminar flow between two stationary parallel plates, the velocity distribution is parabolic, and the maximum velocity (at the midpoint) is 1.5 times the average velocity.

q: 36. The value of the kinetic energy correction factor (α) for the viscous flow through a circular pipe is
explain: The kinetic energy correction factor (α) accounts for the non-uniform velocity distribution. For laminar (viscous) flow in a circular pipe, α is equal to 2.0.

q: 37. The value of the momentum correction factor (β) for the viscous flow through a circular pipe is
explain: The momentum correction factor (β) for laminar flow in a circular pipe is calculated as 4/3, which is approximately 1.33.

q: 38. Hydraulic gradient line (H.G.L.) represents the sum of
options: pressure head, kinetic head and datum head
explain: The Hydraulic Gradient Line (HGL) connects points representing the Piezometric Head, which is the sum of the Pressure Head (p/w) and the Datum Head (z).

q: 39. Total Energy Line (T.E.L.) represents the sum of
options: pressure head, kinetic head and datum head
explain: The Total Energy Line (TEL) represents the total head of the fluid, which is the sum of Pressure Head (p/w), Datum Head (z), and Velocity/Kinetic Head (V²/2g).

q: 40. Mach number is defined as the ratio of
options: viscous force to surface tension force
explain: Mach number is a dimensionless parameter representing the ratio of the inertia force to the elastic force (or the ratio of the velocity of the fluid to the velocity of sound in that fluid).

q: 41. Models are known undistorted model, if
options: prototype and model have different scale ratios
prototype and model have same scale ratio
model and prototype are kinematically similar
explain: An undistorted model is one that is geometrically similar to its prototype, meaning the scale ratio for all linear dimensions (length, width, height) is the same.

q: 42. Geometric similarity between model and prototype means
explain: Geometric similarity exists when the ratio of all corresponding linear dimensions in the model and prototype are equal.

q: 43. Kinematic similarity between model and prototype means
explain: Kinematic similarity means the similarity of motion; it occurs when the ratios of velocities and accelerations at corresponding points in the model and prototype are equal.

q: 44. Dynamic similarity between model and prototype means
explain: Dynamic similarity is the similarity of forces; it exists when the ratios of corresponding forces (inertia, viscous, gravity, etc.) at corresponding points are the same.

q: 45. Mach number (M) is given by
explain: The Mach number is the ratio of the local flow velocity (V) to the local speed of sound (C) in that medium.

q: 46. A body is called stream-lined body when it is placed in a flow and the surface
options: does not coincide with the streamlines
explain: A streamlined body is shaped such that its surface aligns with the streamlines of the flow, minimizing separation and pressure drag.

q: 47. The skin friction drag on a sphere (for Reynolds number less than 0.2) is equal to
explain: In Stokes' flow (Re < 0.2), the total drag is 6πηrv. Mathematically, 2/3 of this is due to skin friction and 1/3 is due to pressure.

q: 48. The pressure drag on a sphere (for Reynolds number less than 0.2) is equal to
explain: As derived in Stokes' law, for very low Reynolds numbers, pressure drag accounts for exactly one-third of the total resistance force.

q: 49. If the depth of flow along the length of the channel is constant, then flow is known as
explain: Uniform flow in an open channel occurs when the depth, discharge, and velocity remain constant at every section along the channel's length.

q: 50. If the depth of flow along the length of the channel is a variable, then flow is known as
explain: Non-uniform flow (or varied flow) occurs when the depth of flow changes from one section to another along the channel.
